title: Selective breeding
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What is the difference between natural and artificial selection?
Can selective breeding create entirely new genes?
How is selective breeding different from genetic engineering?

explain.say: Selective breeding is when humans choose which plants or animals survive.

items: Step 1: Observe variation in a group
Step 3: Breed only the best individuals

explain.say: We look at natural variation first, like different colours in a group.
Next, we must choose the specific traits we want to see more often.
Then, we only let the chosen individuals reproduce to keep the trait going.
For example, farmers selectively breed cows for milk production.
In everyday life, think about dogs bred for specific jobs, like herding.

items: Herding dogs are bred for control
Dogs for companionship have different traits

faq.q: Does selective breeding change the genes themselves?
faq.a: No, it does not change the actual genes. It only increases the chance that certain traits appear.
asks: Are genes physically changed by breeding?

faq.q: Is selective breeding the same as genetic engineering?
faq.a: No, genetic engineering moves genes between species. Selective breeding only uses traits already present in the species.
asks: What is the difference between breeding and engineering?
Can we move genes with breeding?

faq.q: Does this process take a long time?
faq.a: Yes, it takes many generations of careful selection to see big changes.
asks: How long does it take to breed something new?

faq.q: Can we breed for traits that are not visible?
faq.a: It is very difficult, but scientists try to select for traits that affect internal health or behaviour.
asks: Can we select for invisible traits?
What if the trait is internal?

faq.q: What is the main source of variation we use?
faq.a: The main source is random natural variation that already exists within the population.
asks: Where do the good traits come from?
Is variation created by the breeder?

facts: Selective breeding relies on existing variation within a population.
Humans choose the parents, not the genes themselves.
The process takes many generations to show major changes.
It is different from genetic engineering because no genes are moved between species.

quiz.say: To make a dog that never barks, what is the most important first step?

options.show: Wait until the trait naturally disappears.
options.say: Wait until the trait naturally disappears.

options.show: Identify the trait you want to eliminate.
options.say: Identify the trait you want to eliminate.

options.show: Introduce a new gene from another dog.
options.say: Introduce a new gene from another dog.

quiz.why: You must first look at the current variation to know what you are selecting against.

wrong.0: This is passive and does not involve active human selection.
wrong.2: This skips the observation step and assumes the desired trait is obvious.
wrong.3: This describes genetic engineering, not selective breeding.

quiz.say: Farmers want apples that are both sweet and resistant to blight. Which step is crucial?

options.show: Wait for one apple to magically become perfect.
options.say: Wait for one apple to magically become perfect.

options.show: Selecting parents that show both traits together.
options.say: Selecting parents that show both traits together.

options.show: Plant seeds from the sweetest apples only.
options.say: Plant seeds from the sweetest apples only.

options.show: Spray the blight off the apples before breeding.
options.say: Spray the blight off the apples before breeding.

quiz.why: You must select for the combination of traits you want in one generation.

wrong.0: Evolutionary changes require repeated selection over time.
wrong.2: This ignores the blight resistance trait completely.
wrong.3: This is a chemical fix, not a biological selection method.

quiz.say: If a plant has seeds that are yellow, green, or red, and you want red seeds, what must you do?

options.show: Only plant the seeds from the red-seeded plants.
options.say: Only plant the seeds from the red-seeded plants.

options.show: Cross the yellow and green seeds together.
options.say: Cross the yellow and green seeds together.

options.show: Wait for the seeds to change colour naturally.
options.say: Wait for the seeds to change colour naturally.

quiz.why: This is the direct action of selection: choosing only the desired variation.

wrong.1: This loses the chance to increase the frequency of the red trait.
wrong.2: This mixes traits without ensuring the desired outcome.
wrong.3: Natural change is unpredictable and slow.
